title: Research Methods in Psychology Adventure 2: Non-experimental Methods
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet correlational, observational and case study methods.
meta_desc: Psychology Research Methods: correlational, observational and case study methods.
final_note: You contrasted three non-experimental methods and their strengths and limits.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Measures two variables and looks at how they co-vary.

Coefficient r: −1 (perfect negative), 0 (none), +1 (perfect positive).

Strength: useful for ethically unmanipulable variables (smoking & lung cancer).

Crucial caveat: correlation is not causation — third variables, reverse causation.

Types: naturalistic (real setting) vs controlled; covert vs overt; participant vs non-participant.

Festinger's 'When Prophecy Fails' (1956) was covert participant observation.

Pros: high ecological validity; Cons: observer bias, ethics of covert work.

An in-depth look at one person, group or event.

Famous: HM (Milner), Phineas Gage, Genie (1970s feral child).

Strengths: rich data on rare cases; Weaknesses: hard to generalise, researcher bias, often retrospective.
